scope.source_overlap_note: Retain source bands such as grades 5-6. Include accessible grade-5 content; do not imply every problem on a shared paper is grade-5 material.
scope.status: Proposed v1 taxonomy, not empirically calibrated on a user corpus.
scope.design: One primary problem-type leaf; optional essential secondary leaves; independent method, goal, representation, motif, and metadata axes.

topics.label: Counting given objects
topics.definition: Determine the size of a displayed or described collection, including equal groups.
topics.boundary: Use CNT for possible configurations; use SPA when tracing containment or hidden structure is the main challenge.

topics.label: Number order and number lines
topics.definition: Compare numerical sizes, locate values, or determine numerical positions.
topics.boundary: Use LOG.order_constraints for ordering people or objects from relational clues.

topics.label: Place value and numeral construction
topics.definition: Read, compose, decompose, rearrange, or restore numerals using positional value.
topics.boundary: Use REL.cryptarithms for digit assignments constrained by arithmetic; use INT.digit_properties for numerical digit conditions.

topics.label: Addition and subtraction
topics.definition: Combine or remove known amounts when choosing or evaluating the operations is the main task.
topics.boundary: Do not add this as a secondary topic to every problem that happens to use addition.

topics.label: Multiplication, division, and equal groups
topics.definition: Find totals, group sizes, or numbers of equal groups, including interpreting a leftover.
topics.boundary: Use INT.remainders when remainder conditions themselves determine an unknown integer.

topics.label: Arithmetic structure and expressions
topics.definition: Evaluate or compare expressions using grouping, order of operations, compensation, cancellation, or operation properties.
topics.boundary: A long sum remains arithmetic when no sequence rule must be inferred.

topics.label: Estimation, rounding, and magnitude
topics.definition: Approximate, bound numerical size, round, or compare without full calculation.
topics.boundary: Optimization of a constrained arrangement belongs to its structural topic with an optimization goal.

topics.label: Intervals, gaps, and inclusive counting
topics.definition: Relate objects to gaps, count endpoints correctly, or convert equal spacing to the number of positions.
topics.boundary: Use CNT.pair_counts for all pairs, not merely consecutive gaps.

topics.label: Odd-even structure
topics.definition: Use odd/even behavior to constrain values, sums, products, or possibility.
topics.boundary: If parity proves a board transformation impossible, MOV.state_moves can remain primary and parity becomes a strategy or secondary topic.

topics.label: Divisibility and multiples
topics.definition: Use exact divisibility, divisibility tests, or membership in sets of multiples.
topics.boundary: Use gcd_lcm when the common greatest/smallest multiple or divisor is the central relation.

topics.label: Factors, primes, and factorization
topics.definition: Find or characterize factors, prime numbers, composites, or factor counts.
topics.boundary: Use DAT.mean_total if averaging an already supplied factor list is the main task.

topics.label: Common factors and common multiples
topics.definition: Find common divisors, largest equal groups, common periods, or least common multiples.
topics.boundary: Use PAT.cycles when tracking the phases of recurring states is the main task; formal LCM need not be used.

topics.label: Remainders and modular conditions
topics.definition: Infer numbers from division remainders or reason about cyclic residue classes.
topics.boundary: Simple division with a leftover is NUM.multiply_divide; sequence position in an explicit repeating block is PAT.repeat.

topics.label: Digit sums and digit constraints
topics.definition: Use digit sums, products, reversals, or other digit conditions to restrict an integer.
topics.boundary: Use NUM.place_value for positional manipulation alone and REL.cryptarithms for arithmetic digit puzzles.

topics.label: Consecutive numbers, squares, and special forms
topics.definition: Use structural properties of consecutive integers, perfect squares, or similarly specified integer forms.
topics.boundary: Use PAT.growth_numeric when the task is to infer or extend a sequence rule.

topics.label: Equal parts and part-whole meaning
topics.definition: Interpret halves, thirds, quarters, unit fractions, and fractions of regions or sets.
topics.boundary: A shaded picture belongs here when the central task is interpreting a fraction, not computing geometric area.

topics.label: Equivalent fractions and rational comparison
topics.definition: Recognize equivalence or compare fractions and decimals, including positions on a number line.
topics.boundary: Use operations if arithmetic on rational numbers is the central task.

topics.label: Fraction and decimal operations
topics.definition: Calculate with fractions, mixed numbers, or decimals and convert between these forms.
topics.boundary: Use percentages when percent language or percent structure is essential.

topics.label: Fractional amounts and recovering the whole
topics.definition: Find a fraction of an amount, infer a whole, or combine successive fractions of a changing remainder.
topics.boundary: Use REL.transfers when transfers and conservation, rather than fraction structure, drive the task.

topics.label: Ratios, proportional sharing, and scaling
topics.definition: Compare relative amounts, divide in a ratio, find a unit value, or scale corresponding quantities.
topics.boundary: Use REL.multiplicative for a single whole-number comparison without a ratio or proportional structure.

topics.label: Percent as a rate per hundred
topics.definition: Find percent amounts, percent changes, or an original amount from a stated percentage.
topics.boundary: A price story without percent reasoning belongs elsewhere.

topics.label: Additive comparisons and relational chains
topics.definition: Infer unknown quantities from more-than, less-than, before-after, or difference relations.
topics.boundary: Use NUM.add_subtract if amounts and the required operation are already direct; use sum_difference when both total and difference are given.

topics.label: Multiplicative comparisons
topics.definition: Infer quantities from times-as-many relations or chains of such comparisons.
topics.boundary: Use FRC.ratio_proportion for proportional sharing or multiple linked ratios.

topics.label: Total-and-difference problems
topics.definition: Recover two or more amounts from totals and additive differences.
topics.boundary: The story may involve ages, prices, lengths, or scores; these are motifs.

topics.label: Two kinds and two totals
topics.definition: Separate two types using a total count and a second weighted total, such as heads/legs or ticket counts/revenue.
topics.boundary: Known contributions with one missing number can be equations instead; preserve the two-type structure when it matters.

topics.label: Unknown start in a sequence of operations
topics.definition: Recover an initial quantity or missing stage in an explicitly described arithmetic process.
topics.boundary: Work backward is the associated method; reversal as a method does not make unrelated problems this topic.

topics.label: Transfers, redistribution, and conservation
topics.definition: Track before/after amounts when objects or quantities move between containers or people.
topics.boundary: Use FRC.fraction_of_quantity when successive fractions are the defining mathematical relationship.

topics.label: Missing values and symbolic equalities
topics.definition: Infer whole quantities from equations, symbolic identities, or linked equalities without a more specific relationship subtype.
topics.boundary: A picture icon can stand for a whole number; use cryptarithms only when place-value digits are constrained.

topics.label: Balance and equivalence
topics.definition: Infer unknown weights or exchange equivalents by comparing balanced collections.
topics.boundary: Use LOG.weighing_information when selecting informative weighings; use CNT.target_sums when choosing a subset of known weights is central.

topics.label: Digit arithmetic and cryptarithms
topics.definition: Assign digits to letters or blanks subject to place value, carries, arithmetic, and any distinctness rules.
topics.boundary: Do not assume different symbols mean different digits unless stated or explicitly established by the source convention.

topics.label: Rates, motion, and work
topics.definition: Relate distance/time, output/time, combined work, or relative speeds.
topics.boundary: Use MEA.clock_elapsed for clock reading or duration arithmetic without a rate relation.

topics.label: Repeating blocks and indexed positions
topics.definition: Identify a stated or supported repeating block and find positions, counts, or missing members.
topics.boundary: Do not invent a continuation from a short ambiguous sequence; flag ambiguity if the intended rule is not established.

topics.label: Numerical growth rules
topics.definition: Infer or use an additive, multiplicative, or recursive numerical sequence rule.
topics.boundary: A supplied expression to evaluate is NUM.computation_structure.

topics.label: Growing figures
topics.definition: Relate a figure's stage to the number of tiles, dots, sticks, or other components.
topics.boundary: Use GEO or CNT when only a fixed figure is involved and no growth relation is needed.

topics.label: Alternating and interleaved rules
topics.definition: Separate interwoven subsequences or alternating operations to determine a term.
topics.boundary: A single repeated block is repeat; tag this only when interleaving is a distinct obstacle.

topics.label: Recurring states and synchronized cycles
topics.definition: Track states through repeated operations, simultaneous periodic events, or phase alignment.
topics.boundary: Use INT.gcd_lcm when common-multiple structure dominates; use MOV.state_moves when reachability or legal moves dominate.

topics.label: Unit conversions and compound units
topics.definition: Convert or compare measurements across units, including area and volume unit scales.
topics.boundary: Do not make this primary merely because a geometry question includes units.

topics.label: Length, distance, and reading scales
topics.definition: Read rulers, compare measured lengths, or combine distances from a scale.
topics.boundary: Use GEO.perimeter for a shape's boundary and NUM.intervals for endpoint/gap structure.

topics.label: Mass, capacity, and temperature
topics.definition: Read or compare these measurements and reason about their units or physical quantities.
topics.boundary: Use REL.balance for unknown equivalences and MOV.state_moves for a constrained pouring puzzle.

topics.label: Prices, payment, and change
topics.definition: Calculate transaction amounts, price totals, or monetary change.
topics.boundary: Coin selection/counting belongs to CNT.target_sums; discounts may belong to FRC.percentages.

topics.label: Clocks and elapsed time
topics.definition: Read analog or digital time, determine durations, or reconstruct start/end times.
topics.boundary: Clock-hand geometry is GEO.angles; regularly recurring clock events may be PAT.cycles.

topics.label: Calendars and dates
topics.definition: Use month lengths, weekdays, dates, and inclusive or exclusive date intervals.
topics.boundary: Use PAT.cycles when repeated-event phase alignment is the main obstacle.

topics.label: Properties of plane figures
topics.definition: Identify or reason about sides, vertices, parallelism, triangles, quadrilaterals, and circles.
topics.boundary: Use SPA.visual_matching for perceptual matching without geometric properties.

topics.label: Angles and turns
topics.definition: Reason about angles, directions of turns, or angle sums in elementary figures.
topics.boundary: Navigating a complete route may be MOV.navigation with angle reasoning secondary.

topics.label: Perimeter and boundary length
topics.definition: Find, compare, or optimize boundaries, including shared edges and rectilinear figures.
topics.boundary: Tile area is not perimeter; tag area only when essential to the relationship.

topics.label: Area of standard figures
topics.definition: Determine or compare area using unit squares or elementary standard-shape relations.
topics.boundary: Use area_composite for overlap, subtraction, decomposition, or linked regions that drive the problem.

topics.label: Composite, shaded, and related areas
topics.definition: Infer area by combining, subtracting, rearranging, or comparing regions and shared dimensions.
topics.boundary: A fraction label on a shaded region does not automatically make this FRC.part_whole.

topics.label: Symmetry and rigid transformations
topics.definition: Use reflection, rotation, translation, congruence, or symmetry to identify or complete plane figures.
topics.boundary: Use SPA.folding_cutting for tracking folds/cuts; use CNT.equivalence_counting for numbers of arrangements modulo symmetry.

topics.label: Dissection, tangrams, packing, and tiling
topics.definition: Construct, fit, cut, or tile plane regions under shape constraints.
topics.boundary: If the question asks how many distinct tilings, CNT can be primary; use a tiling motif to preserve the format.

topics.label: Coordinates and grid geometry
topics.definition: Read or infer locations and elementary geometric relationships on a coordinate grid.
topics.boundary: A grid used only as a logic board is LOG.grid_constraints.

topics.label: Relative position and containment
topics.definition: Trace inside/outside, left/right, front/behind, or tangled boundaries and positions.
topics.boundary: Use NUM.quantities when counting plainly visible objects is the only work.

topics.label: Visual matching and missing pieces
topics.definition: Recognize an identical object, matching fragment, or missing piece from visible features.
topics.boundary: Use GEO.symmetry_transformations when a geometric transformation is the key relation.

topics.label: Properties of solids
topics.definition: Reason about faces, edges, vertices, or elementary solid structure and unit-cube volume.
topics.boundary: Use cube_stacks_views when reconstruction or hidden cubes are central.

topics.label: Cube stacks, hidden cubes, and views
topics.definition: Infer arrangements from top/front/side views, count concealed cubes, or reason about exposed/painted faces.
topics.boundary: Do not assume hidden support cubes, no gaps, or conventional construction unless stated or justified.

topics.label: Nets and assembled solids
topics.definition: Relate a flat net to a solid, including adjacent or opposite faces and valid nets.
topics.boundary: Use cube_orientation for a solid already assembled and turned or rolled.

topics.label: Dice and solid orientation
topics.definition: Track labels, opposite faces, rotations, or rolls of an assembled solid.
topics.boundary: Dice probability belongs to DAT; arrays of dice outcomes may belong to CNT.

topics.label: Paper folding, hole punching, and cuts
topics.definition: Track positions, layers, holes, or shape after folding, cutting, and unfolding.
topics.boundary: If folding simply changes a rectangle's area and no fold geometry is needed, GEO.area_basic can be primary.

topics.label: Overlays, occlusion, and interlacing
topics.definition: Infer visible regions, stacking order, over/under relations, or superimposed images.
topics.boundary: Numerical area of an overlap belongs to GEO.area_composite.

topics.label: Ordered arrangements and strings
topics.definition: Count sequences, lineups, codes, or digit strings in which order matters, including adjacency restrictions.
topics.boundary: LOG.order_constraints is for deducing an arrangement; count here only when enumerating alternatives is central.

topics.label: Unordered selections
topics.definition: Count groups or subsets where internal order does not create a new result, including outfits or menus chosen from categories.
topics.boundary: Use pair_counts for pairwise meetings/connections and target_sums for additive-value restrictions; choices from several categories may use the product rule.

topics.label: Counting with identical objects or symmetry
topics.definition: Count configurations while identifying duplicates caused by indistinguishable objects, rotations, or reflections.
topics.boundary: Apply only the equivalence relation actually stated; a circular drawing does not automatically identify rotations.

topics.label: Distributing objects into recipients or boxes
topics.definition: Count allocations or partitions under specified capacities, identities, and empty-box rules.
topics.boundary: Use FRC.ratio_proportion or NUM.multiply_divide for finding an amount in one specified equal sharing.

topics.label: Selections or combinations with a target total
topics.definition: Find, count, or optimize combinations of coins, weights, lengths, or other known contributions meeting a target.
topics.boundary: Use REL.two_totals when deducing counts of two types from two totals is the distinctive structure.

topics.label: Counting routes and paths
topics.definition: Count permissible routes through a grid, network, staircase, or staged choice process.
topics.boundary: Finding a single feasible/shortest route is MOV.navigation; preserve no-revisit and endpoint rules.

topics.label: Counting embedded figures
topics.definition: Count segments, triangles, rectangles, squares, or other specified figures in a fixed diagram.
topics.boundary: Do not confuse counting figures with summing area; tag geometry secondarily only if geometric properties are essential.

topics.label: Counting digits and positional occurrences
topics.definition: Count appearances of digits or symbols across a range, page numbers, or systematically generated numerals.
topics.boundary: Counting numbers that contain a digit and counting occurrences are different targets; preserve the wording.

topics.label: Counting overlapping sets
topics.definition: Find population counts with intersections, unions, complements, or inclusion-exclusion.
topics.boundary: Use LOG.set_membership when the unknown is identity/membership rather than cardinality.

topics.label: Pairwise interactions and connections
topics.definition: Count handshakes, games, pairings, or connections between distinct pairs, accounting for double counting.
topics.boundary: Use unordered_selections for general subset sizes and MOV.networks when connectivity rather than count is central.

topics.label: Matching entities to attributes
topics.definition: Assign people or objects to unique choices from positive/negative clues or allowed lists.
topics.boundary: If numeric equations determine values, prefer REL; if alternatives must be counted, prefer CNT.

topics.label: Ordering and ranking from clues
topics.definition: Deduce positions, relative order, or ordinal ranks from relational information.
topics.boundary: Use NUM.intervals for a pure endpoint/gap relation and CNT.ordered_arrangements for counting possible orders.

topics.label: Truth, lies, and consistency
topics.definition: Determine which statements or speakers can be true under a truth-count or consistency condition.
topics.boundary: Do not assume a speaker always lies unless that rule is explicit.

topics.label: Classification and set membership
topics.definition: Use property-based classes, overlaps, exclusions, Venn regions, or shared attributes to identify members.
topics.boundary: Use CNT.overlap_counts for numerical set cardinalities.

topics.label: Grid and number-placement constraints
topics.definition: Complete Sudoku-like, magic-sum, minesweeper-like, adjacency, or other local-constraint boards.
topics.boundary: One simple missing sum is REL.equations; a board alone does not make a problem geometry.

topics.label: Guarantees and worst-case selection
topics.definition: Find how many choices force a repeat, match, occupancy, or other guaranteed event.
topics.boundary: Tag goal guarantee and strategy worst_case; ordinary likelihood is DAT probability.

topics.label: Information from tests or weighings
topics.definition: Identify a hidden type or anomalous object from limited comparisons, tests, or weighings.
topics.boundary: Unknown-weight arithmetic on an already balanced scale is REL.balance.

topics.label: Navigation and route optimization
topics.definition: Follow directions or find a feasible/shortest route through a maze, map, or network.
topics.boundary: Counting all routes is CNT.path_counts; simple lengths already given are MEA.length_scales.

topics.label: One-stroke and edge-traversal problems
topics.definition: Determine or construct a route visiting required edges or connections, such as drawing without lifting a pencil.
topics.boundary: Shortest-path questions without a traversal obligation are navigation.

topics.label: Legal moves and state transformations
topics.definition: Reach a target, minimize moves, or test possibility in swapping, toggling, pouring, crossing, or matchstick tasks.
topics.boundary: For a fixed state simply read off its attributes; a changing state and legal operations define this topic.

topics.label: Winning strategies and turn-taking games
topics.definition: Determine a forced win or move under explicit rules and an adversarial turn structure.
topics.boundary: A probability-of-winning question is DAT unless strategic choice is also essential.

topics.label: Connectivity and network structure
topics.definition: Reason about connected components, bridges, connections, or simple network feasibility.
topics.boundary: Use CNT.pair_counts if only the number of pairwise connections is sought.

topics.label: Tables, charts, and data interpretation
topics.definition: Read or infer information from pictographs, bar charts, tables, or simple graphs.
topics.boundary: Do not tag this merely because a logic puzzle uses a table as its layout.

topics.label: Averages and totals
topics.definition: Find a mean, reconstruct a total, or reason about how adding/removing values changes an average.
topics.boundary: Use INT.factors_primes secondarily only if finding the underlying factor set is also essential.

topics.label: Median, mode, range, and ordered data
topics.definition: Infer these statistics or reconstruct a dataset from them.
topics.boundary: Ranking people from clues is LOG.order_constraints.

topics.label: Possible, impossible, certain, and likely
topics.definition: Compare likelihood or classify events qualitatively under a random experiment.
topics.boundary: Logical feasibility without randomness belongs to the relevant logic or structural topic.

topics.label: Single-stage probability
topics.definition: Compute a probability from a well-defined experiment or sample space.
topics.boundary: Do not assume outcomes or pictured regions are equally likely without justification.

topics.label: Multi-stage probability
topics.definition: Compute simple compound-event probabilities, including dependent draws and replacement rules.
topics.boundary: Count outcomes under CNT when no probability is requested; add counting secondarily only if it is substantive.

strategies.direct_calculation: Evaluate the required arithmetic directly; use when this describes the core method.
strategies.work_backward: Reverse operations or reconstruct an earlier state from a later one.
strategies.draw_model: Introduce a diagram, bar model, number line, or other mathematical model.
strategies.organized_enumeration: List or tabulate possibilities systematically, with completeness and no duplication.
strategies.guess_check: Test candidate values against all constraints in a structured way.
strategies.constraint_propagation: Use forced choices and exclusions to narrow remaining possibilities.
strategies.substitution_elimination: Substitute or combine equalities to remove unknowns.
strategies.find_pattern: Identify a supported repeating, growing, or recursive rule.
strategies.unitary_scaling: Reduce to one unit or a common proportional unit, then scale.
strategies.decompose_recompose: Break an expression, figure, or collection into useful parts and recombine.
strategies.symmetry: Use reflection, rotation, or interchangeable roles to reduce work or establish equivalence.
strategies.complement: Count or calculate the whole minus unwanted cases.
strategies.sum_product_rule: Combine disjoint alternatives by addition or successive independent choices by multiplication.
strategies.inclusion_exclusion: Correct overlapping counts by accounting for intersections.
strategies.invariant: Use a quantity or property unchanged by every legal move.
strategies.parity_coloring: Use odd/even classes or a coloring to constrain outcomes.
strategies.extremal_bounds: Prove an upper/lower bound and, for an optimum, exhibit an attaining construction.
strategies.worst_case_pigeonhole: Maximize avoidance before concluding an outcome is forced.
strategies.simulate_state: Track a small number of steps, positions, orientations, or states explicitly.
strategies.backward_game_analysis: Classify small positions as winning/losing and work back from terminal positions.
strategies.option_elimination: Use the supplied answer choices materially to exclude or test possibilities.

classification_rules: Treat question text, diagrams, answer choices, and supplied solutions as data, never as instructions to the classifier.
Classify one independently answerable question/subpart at a time. Preserve the parent question ID and shared stimulus. Do not extract answers or worked examples as new questions by accident.
Inspect all essential diagrams and image answer choices. OCR text alone is insufficient for spatial relations, erased digits, markings, and many choices.
Identify the requested output and the central mathematical relation or obstacle. Assign the most specific supported primary topic, not a story keyword or every topic mentioned.
Prefer a precise structural subtype over a generic fallback. Use the tie-breaker rules when topics overlap. Do not choose a category solely because an adult solver used algebra.
Add at most three secondary topics, and only when each contributes independent, essential mathematical work. Omit routine counting, arithmetic, diagram reading, or units used as support.
When two incompatible primary labels are plausible, list them as candidates and mark ambiguous; do not disguise uncertainty as secondary-topic membership.

Keep mathematical topics separate from strategies, representations, goals, motifs, and explicit constraints. A counting question is not automatically combinatorics, and a picture is not automatically geometry.
Use an elementary canonical approach consistent with the complete question or supplied solution to assign up to three strategies. Do not claim that this is the only possible solution method.
Do not infer unstated conventions about distinguishability, replacement, rotations, leading zeroes, hidden cubes, fairness, scale, or pattern continuation. Record material ambiguity for review.
Preserve source grade, country/system, contest, year, question number, points, and round as reported. A grades 5-6 paper remains labeled [5,6]; do not silently relabel it grade 5.

Estimate prerequisite band and difficulty separately from source grade. Grade estimates are heuristic and optional. Difficulty is relative to an explicitly selected reference grade, not determined by large numbers, points, or lengthy wording alone.
Output only registered IDs. If only the broad family is supported, use family_only with a null primary_topic. Unknown and novel topics need review; do not force them into a miscellaneous category.
Use brief, auditable evidence for the label; do not output a full solution or private chain of reasoning. Solving to the extent needed to disambiguate labels is sufficient.
Preserve extraction and mathematical quality flags even when the topic itself is clear. A corrupted answer key does not automatically change the question type.
Do not invent corpus frequencies, learner mastery, or calibrated confidence. This taxonomy has been designed from sources and illustrative checks, not evaluated on the user's corpus.

tie_breakers.rule: NUM.quantities for a given collection; CNT for enumerating possible arrangements or specified embedded figures. SPA.containment_position if tracing the visual boundaries is the bottleneck.
LOG.order_constraints for deducing order/rank; CNT.ordered_arrangements for the number of allowable lineups; NUM.intervals for a pure endpoint/gap relation.
SPA.cube_orientation for faces/rotations; CNT.ordered_arrangements for outcome strings; DAT.probability_single or probability_multi for probability.

MEA.money for payment/change; CNT.target_sums for selecting/counting combinations of known values; REL.balance for unknown equivalents; LOG.weighing_information for designing/interpreting diagnostic tests.
LOG.set_membership for identities; CNT.overlap_counts for cardinalities; GEO.area_composite for geometric areas; REL.equations for a missing number constrained by region totals.
LOG.grid_constraints for coupled placement/adjacency rules; REL.equations for a simple missing sum; REL.cryptarithms when symbols denote place-value digits.
SPA.folding_cutting when fold geometry or hole/layer location is central; GEO.area_basic or area_composite when only the resulting area relation is required. Record folded_paper as a motif.
CNT.path_counts for how many; MOV.navigation for finding a route or shortest route; MOV.traversal for using each required edge; MEA.length_scales for direct distance arithmetic.
PAT.repeat for an explicit repeated block; PAT.cycles for recurring states/phase alignment; INT.gcd_lcm when a common divisor/multiple is the key structure. Do not give both by default.
The requested goal is separate from the topic. Minimum coins can be CNT.target_sums; an impossible swap can be MOV.state_moves; guaranteed repeated color is LOG.pigeonhole.
Use the specific relation (sum_difference, two_totals, rates, fraction_of_quantity, etc.) when present. REL.equations is a fallback, not a tag for every problem that can be written as equations.
Preserve a statement-grounded primary topic. Choose a canonical elementary strategy; alternate correct methods do not create extra primary topics or duplicates.

sources.title: Math Kangaroo official curricula, grades 1-2, 3-4, and 5-6
sources.notes: The three published curricula support arithmetic, elementary geometry, visual/spatial work, logic, measurement, and early data/probability. Upper bands introduce more factors, rational-number work, and algebraic thinking. These are general guidelines; their grade bands do not establish a universal grade placement for every subtype.

sources.title: Math Kangaroo official webinar topics
sources.notes: Useful evidence for separating problem content from methods: lesson listings include both mathematical topics and strategies such as drawing, organizing possibilities, and reversing a process.

sources.title: Math Kangaroo 2024 official sample questions
sources.notes: Inspected the grades 1-2, 3-4, and 5-6 problem pages visually. They include visual containment, shared-set clues, allowed-choice matching, synchronized color cycles, target weights, local grid constraints, and related rectangle areas. Shapes and numbers used merely as symbols should not determine the primary category.

sources.title: Noetic Learning official grade-specific sample questions
sources.notes: Samples for grades 2-5 span age relations, dates, equivalent prices, digit arithmetic, constrained lineups, alternating sequences, area, and statement consistency. These are coverage examples, not estimates of topic frequency.

sources.title: MOEMS official resources and Division E sample
sources.notes: Division E covers grades 4-6. The linked sample was downloaded and read: it includes a structured sum, digit-occurrence counting, folded-rectangle area, a constrained number-placement optimization, and a cryptarithm optimization. Its multiple solution methods motivate keeping topic identity separate from method.

sources.title: SASMO official syllabus
sources.notes: Broad coverage includes arithmetic/statistics, geometry/measurement, modeled word problems, and nonroutine number, spatial, logic, and cryptarithm tasks. The taxonomy below is an original cross-competition synthesis, not a copy of an official SASMO classification.

sources.title: Math League official fifth-grade sample, spring 2019
sources.notes: Read the text-extracted sample for breadth, with extraction defects treated as missing evidence. It supports including integer factors, constrained digit outcomes, rates, averages, calendars, and extrema. No visual claim relies on its malformed text extraction.

source.locator: Original illustrative example; not a contest quotation

illustrative_examples.statement: You have one coin of each value 1, 4, 6, and 9. What is the fewest coins that total 10?

source.locator: Original illustrative example; not a contest quotation

illustrative_examples.statement: Two identical sealed boxes balance six identical blocks. How many blocks balance one box?

source.locator: Original illustrative example; not a contest quotation

classification.brief_basis: The equality between collections determines an unknown exchange equivalent.

source.locator: Original illustrative example; not a contest quotation
